corrected_value.title: Promoting positive feelings and motivation for language learning: The role of a confidence-building diary.

decisions.quote:
In the original study, 

the tool was demonstrated to be “effective […] for promoting positive feelings and 

supporting students’ basic psychological needs” (Shelton-Strong & Mynard, 2021, p. 1). In 

the replication study, three factors were considered to validate the efficacy of the CBD, 

namely: i) students’ active and autonomous engagement in language learning activities; ii) 

the prevalent emergence of positive feelings; iii) students’ motivation, investigated also 

through the identification of basic personal needs.
decisions.reason: Although the narrative overview co-cites Shelton-Strong and Mynard (2018, 2021) when referring to the singular 'original study', Table 1 ('Original Study (Shelton-Strong & Mynard, 2021)'), the shared research questions (RQ1–RQ3), the adapted diary example, the emergent coding scheme, and the specific original finding re-tested in the Findings section all identify Shelton-Strong and Mynard (2021) as the primary empirical report being replicated, while the 2018 Relay Journal article is not separately re-tested and Spricigo (2023) is the co-author's master's thesis reporting this replication.

decisions.quote:
In the original study, all the participants felt that the CBD-based intervention was 

beneficial. In the replication study, although the CBD was generally well-received, a minority 

of participants did not find it motivating.
decisions.reason: The paper does not merely apply the diary descriptively without comparison; it directly compares results against Shelton-Strong and Mynard (2021) on shared research questions RQ1–RQ3. No overarching verdict claims that all original findings replicated (the conclusion endorses the tool's utility for awareness, positive feelings, and basic psychological need satisfaction and calls the data 'promising'). Across the shared RQ comparisons (setting aside new modification-specific extensions on schedule duration, layout personalization, and Italian curriculum feasibility), the authors report agreement on out-of-class activity context, positive mindset/feelings, and SDT basic psychological needs (competence, autonomy, relatedness), but explicitly contrast their results with the original on RQ1 preferred activity types (receptive vs. speaking activities, lines 881-885) and RQ3 motivation (a minority did not find the diary motivating vs. universal benefit in the original, lines 1102-1106), which is 'mixed' under the codebook.

decisions.quote:
Drawing on the literature on self-confidence, motivational theories, and positive psychology 
in the field of language learning, the present paper aspires to contribute to the literature by 
discussing some key findings of a recent conceptual replication study. In the original study, 
Shelton-Strong and Mynard (2018, 2021) investigated the benefits of keeping a diary for 
university language students’ motivation and L2 confidence. The replication study by 
Spricigo (2023) aimed to confirm original findings within a different educational context. For 
this purpose, the research design underwent some necessary modifications justified by the 
need to investigate the efficacy of using diaries among Italian younger students (13-14 years 
old) and the applicability of the teaching intervention in a lower-school context.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding correctly classify this record as a replication: the article reports the empirical conceptual replication study (conducted for co-author Spricigo's 2023 unpublished master's thesis) collecting new data from 42 Italian lower-secondary school students to re-test Shelton-Strong and Mynard's (2021) confidence-building diary intervention findings.
